text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 4.6% today after a brutal week-long selloff that saw the stock down 17% since early November. The rebound came as oil prices steadied (US crude at $99.64/barrel) and refineries continued running near full capacity at 94.5%, suggesting solid demand for refined products like gasoline and diesel. The worst of the panic selling appears to have paused, at least temporarily.

The prior week's sharp decline was likely driven by political shifts: Democratic gains in the midterm elections raised investor concerns about stricter environmental regulation and a potential pivot toward renewable energy investments rather than fossil fuels. Today's bounce may reflect either profit-taking after the steep drop or a reassessment of near-term refining fundamentals, which remain solid with healthy inventory levels and high utilization rates still in place.
